metric.why: A hall can be full by power and half empty by space, or the reverse. Tracking both per cabinet is how operators find capacity they already own before building more.
metric.metric: Stranded power and space per cabinet
metric.definition: Utility power or floor space that is allocated and paid for but cannot be used, because the other of the pair ran out first or airflow limits were reached.

reading.body:
A data center hall often exhausts one resource before another, leaving power or floor space paid for but unused, and tracking this stranded capacity per cabinet is how operators identify space to reclaim before building new halls.

When power runs out while floor space remains, or space fills while power capacity sits idle, the operator has paid for infrastructure that generates no return. This inefficiency compounds across a portfolio. A facility with high stranded capacity is not using its buildings efficiently, which means the cost per usable unit of compute rises. For AI scaling at grid-constrained timescales, this matters because inefficient use of existing buildings delays the moment when new buildings, and new power connections, become the next bottleneck.

Stranded power and space arise from three sources: uneven demand across cabinets, limits set by airflow and cooling, and the indivisibility of infrastructure components. The metric does not account for the cost of capital tied up in that stranded capacity, nor does it reveal whether an operator can shift workloads to recover the resource. It shows where waste exists, not how quickly it can be reclaimed.
